instruction: Change the subtitle color on slide 2 to red to match the title color.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the subtitle color 'Customer Reviews' on slide 2 from green (0, 128, 0) to red (255, 0, 0) to match the title color. Custom getter extracts subtitle color, custom metric compares against expected red RGB.
metadata.verification: Verified from source file: Slide 2 subtitle 'Customer Reviews' has RGB(0, 128, 0) green color, title has RGB(255, 0, 0) red. Task requires changing subtitle to red.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 1.0 if subtitle color matches red RGB(255, 0, 0) within tolerance of 5, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Getter assumes subtitle is the second text shape in slide.shapes iteration order, but shape order is not guaranteed to be title-first, subtitle-second in PowerPoint/Impress
No validation that the correct text element ('Customer Reviews') is being read - could read any second text shape
Could verify the wrong text shape's color (e.g., title instead of subtitle), leading to incorrect pass/fail results
The logic might work by coincidence in some cases but is semantically unreliable for robust verification
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Identify subtitle by placeholder type (e.g., shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.SUBTITLE) instead of position in iteration order
Or verify by text content matching (check if shape.text contains 'Customer Reviews' to ensure correct element)
Or use slide layout information and placeholder indices to identify the correct text frame
Return both the text content and color from getter to verify that the correct element was checked
Add better error handling for cases where subtitle color cannot be extracted or subtitle is not found
